node_definition.done_when: A test in tests/test_snapshot_loader_keeps_one_instance.py imports reckon.crew.obligation_snapshot, calls the hook's snapshot_module() and the cli loader, and asserts that sys.modules["reckon.crew.obligation_snapshot"], the reckon.crew package attribute and both loaders' return values are one object; it fails at the base revision. The hook keeps loading by path, without importing the crew facade, when nothing has loaded the module yet. Running the hook tests and tests/test_obligations_snapshot_is_published.py in one serial pytest process, in whichever order splits them at base, fails at base and passes at head. The obligations and hook test files are recorded as flat baseline_suite and after_suite records.
node_definition.goal: Keep one instance of reckon.crew.obligation_snapshot per process. The self-diagnosing asserts landed at e2958eaa9 named the cause of both snapshot test failures in a whole-suite run (coordinator log /tmp/claude-39486/-home-ITER-mcintos-Code-reckon/bd47f8f3-7617-4973-86e9-6be0d83c0a53/scratchpad/w74-head.log): "sys.modules holds a different instance" of reckon.crew.obligation_snapshot, its _SWEEPS holding the producer's entry, while the test's instance had none. snapshot_module() in reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py and the loader near reckon/cli.py:3012 each load the module by file path and assign sys.modules["reckon.crew.obligation_snapshot"] unconditionally, so a test that runs one of them after the module was already imported splits the process into two instances. Both loaders must reuse an instance sys.modules already holds, loading by path only when none is loaded.
